body:
Strong +1 on this, with some concrete data from the other side of it.

I've just built and released a Terraform provider for Homarr against the current API: **https://github.com/rfdrew/terraform-provider-homarr** (verified against 1.73.0). It deliberately uses only the OpenAPI surface, not tRPC, since `/api/trpc/…` is an internal detail of the web UI. That turned out to be the deciding constraint, so here is exactly where the current API stops being enough for declarative tooling.

### What already works well

`homarr_app` round-trips perfectly — `POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/apps` is a complete, well-behaved lifecycle, and it made apps the easiest resource to implement. Boards, users, invites and `/api/settings/board` are all usable too. The six routers exported in [`packages/api/src/open-api.ts`](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/dev/packages/api/src/open-api.ts) get you surprisingly far.

### The gap that hurts most: board settings are write-only

`PATCH /api/boards/{id}/settings` exists, but there is no matching `GET`. Everything it writes — `pageTitle`, colours, `opacity`, `itemRadius`, `backgroundImage*`, `customCss`, `disableStatus` — is therefore unreadable over REST.

For Terraform this is worse than a missing feature: without a read path there is no drift detection. My `homarr_board_settings` resource has to record what Terraform last applied and hope it still matches. A change made in the UI is silently kept, and removing an attribute from the config cannot reset it. I had to document it as write-only, which is a bad experience to have to explain to users.

**A single `GET /api/boards/{id}/settings` mirroring the existing PATCH would fix this outright.** It is the highest value-per-effort item on this whole list.

### Tiles: the POST already exists, the other three verbs don't

This one is closer than the issue suggests. `POST /api/boards/items` **is** already exposed over REST ([`board.ts`](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/dev/packages/api/src/router/board.ts) `addItem`), and it works — it auto-places the item and returns `{ itemId }`.

But create-only cannot back a declarative resource. There is no way to list what is on a board, change a tile's options, move or resize it, or delete it. So I could add tiles but never converge on a desired state, and left the capability out rather than ship a resource that can only ever grow a board.

What would make tiles manageable:

| Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/boards/{id}/items` | list items with `kind`, `options`, `integrationIds`, section and grid position |
| `PATCH /api/boards/items/{itemId}` | change `options` / `integrationIds` |
| `DELETE /api/boards/items/{itemId}` | remove a tile |
| position + size on create/update | otherwise layout is not reproducible, only "next free slot" |

With those four, plus the settings `GET` above, a board becomes fully expressible as code — which is what most people in this thread actually want.

### Smaller papercuts

- **`GET /api/boards` omits the column count.** It lives on the layout, which is tRPC-only, so a board's column count can be set at creation and then never read back. In the provider it has to force replacement on change, and import needs a composite `<board_id>,<column_count>` id — a bare id would leave it null and make the next plan destroy the board.
- **`POST /api/users` returns an empty body.** The provider has to create a user and then search `GET /api/users` by name to recover its id. Returning `{ id }` would be a one-line change.
- **`POST /api/users` rejects `"email": null`** while accepting an omitted key or `""`, which is easy to trip over from generated clients.
- **Groups have no REST surface**, so `group_ids` on a user is create-only and unreadable. Even a read-only `GET /api/groups` would help.
- **Integrations have no REST surface**, which is the single most requested thing I expect users to ask me for.

### Confirming the bootstrap problem

Can confirm this is real. There is no REST path through onboarding, so to test the provider in CI I had to script the tRPC endpoints the UI itself calls (`onboard.nextStep`, `user.initUser`, `serverSettings.initSettings`, `onboard.setupIntegrations`) and then sign in through NextAuth just to mint an API key. It works, but it is exactly the kind of thing that breaks on a minor upgrade — precisely because I'm reaching into internals that were never meant to be public.

---

Happy to help however is useful: reviewing endpoint shapes from a Terraform/IaC consumer's perspective, testing against `dev`, or adding provider resources as endpoints land. If it helps prioritise, my order would be:

1. `GET /api/boards/{id}/settings`
2. read/update/delete for board items
3. column count / layout in the board response
4. `GET /api/groups` and integration CRUD

Thanks for Homarr — it's a genuinely nice piece of software, and the API is closer to automatable than this issue implies.

issue.body:
Closes #6435.

## Why

Boards could only be created empty through the API. `POST /api/boards/items` took no geometry, so the size always came from `widgetDefaultSizes` and the position was always the next free cell — a dashboard could not be described in code. Search engines, integrations, groups, api keys and global settings were reachable from the interface only.

## Board composition

`POST /api/boards/items` now accepts an **optional** placement. Without it the behaviour is byte for byte what it was before:

```json
{ "boardId": "...", "kind": "clock", "sectionId": "...", "xOffset": 4, "yOffset": 2, "width": 6, "height": 5 }
```

`width`/`height` set the size, `xOffset`/`yOffset` an exact position, `sectionId` the target section. The values apply to every layout and the width is clamped to narrow breakpoints; a `layouts` array gives per breakpoint control instead. Overlaps are rejected with `400`.

Added around it:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Items | `GET /api/boards/{id}/items`, `PATCH`/`DELETE /api/boards/{boardId}/items/{itemId}` |
| Sections | `GET`/`POST /api/boards/{id}/sections`, `PATCH`/`DELETE .../sections/{sectionId}` |
| Layouts | `GET`/`PUT /api/boards/{id}/layouts` |
| Board | `GET /api/boards/{id}` returns layouts, sections and items at once |
| Access | `GET /api/boards/{id}/permissions`, `PUT .../permissions/users`, `PUT .../permissions/groups` |
| Portability | `GET /api/boards/{id}/export` ⇄ `POST /api/boards/import` with `onConflict: fail｜skip｜replace` |

Ids inside a board document are local references and are remapped on import, so the same document can be applied repeatedly and to other instances.

## Remaining services

Search engines, integrations, groups, api keys and server settings are exposed over OpenAPI and registered as MCP tools. `GET /api/config/export` ⇄ `POST /api/config/import` cover a whole instance.

The configuration document keeps ids as they are — widget options reference other entities by id inside an opaque object, so remapping would silently break boards. Entities are instead matched by natural key when the id is unknown, which is what makes a document from a separately installed instance applicable at all: every instance seeds its own `everyone` group with a random id.

It deliberately contains no users, no group memberships, no secret values, no custom widgets and no media — that is documented, and the backup endpoints remain the way to make a complete copy. Those now accept an `ApiKey` header so a recovery job does not need a browser session.

## Headless bootstrap

`homarr api-keys create -u admin` prints a key without the web interface. Together with the existing `recreate-admin` that removes the last manual step from a first time setup. `api-keys list` and `delete` are there too.

## Safety

- **No database migration.** The schema already stores position and size in `item_layout`.
- **Imports are atomic.** Statements are collected and validated first, then applied in one transaction, so a document with a broken reference never leaves a board half written. `replace` never deletes the board row, so home board settings and per user permissions pointing at it survive.
- **Bounded work.** Grid coordinates and sizes in a document are capped, and the placement scan only tests slot edges and never looks past the last occupied row, so its cost does not depend on the column count.
- **Backwards compatible.** Every new field is optional; existing endpoints keep their behaviour.

## Testing

`pnpm turbo typecheck`, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm format` are clean, docs build passes. 377 tests in the touched packages, including:

- placement: explicit size and position, collisions, clamping to narrow breakpoints, dynamic sections as sub grids, regression on the previous automatic placement
- import/export round trips, `skip`/`replace` idempotency, rollback on an invalid document, cross instance adoption
- authorization: anonymous and unprivileged sessions against every new endpoint, asserting `404` rather than `403` where board existence must not leak

The ten failing files in a full run (`packages/db/test/*-migration`, `packages/integrations/test/*`) are testcontainers based and fail identically on a clean checkout here.

## Notes for review

- Documentation lives in `apps/docs` in this repo, so it is updated in tree rather than in `homarr-labs/documentation`. Happy to move it if that is the wrong place.
- `POST /api/boards/import` keeps the strict board name rule because it creates a board like the interface does; `config/import` accepts any name because it restores. Both are documented.
- The grid cap is 256. It covers oldmarr boards with room to spare, but if wider boards exist in the wild the number should be revisited.

---

- [x] Builds without warnings or errors (`pnpm build`, autofix with `pnpm format:fix`)
- [x] Pull request targets `dev` branch
- [x] Commits follow the [conventional commits guideline](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/)
- [x] No shorthand variable names are used (eg. `x`, `y`, `i` or any abbrevation)
- [x] Documentation is up to date
- [x] When using AI; No temp files are checked in, the code style follows the rest of the project
